definition.def: If you say that someone manipulates people, you disapprove of them because they skilfully force or persuade people to do what they want. [disapproval]
examples: He is a very difficult character. He manipulates people. [VERB noun]
She's always borrowing my clothes and manipulating me to give her money. [VERB noun to-infinitive]
They have kids who manipulate them into buying toys. [VERB noun + into]

definition.def: If you say that someone manipulates an event or situation, you disapprove of them because they use or control it for their own benefit, or cause it to develop in the way they want. [disapproval]
examples: She was unable, for once, to control and manipulate events. [VERB noun]
They felt he had been cowardly in manipulating the system to avoid the draft. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you manipulate something that requires skill, such as a complicated piece of equipment or a difficult idea, you operate it or process it.
examples: The technology uses a pen to manipulate a computer. [VERB noun]
The puppets are expertly manipulated by Liz Walker. [VERB noun]
Much of what I do is manipulating data from different sources. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If someone manipulates your bones or muscles, they skilfully move and press them with their hands in order to push the bones into their correct position or make the muscles less stiff.
examples: The way he can manipulate my leg has helped my arthritis so much. [VERB noun]

definition.def: behaviour that controls or influences somebody/something, often in a dishonest way so that they do not realize it
examples: Advertising like this is a cynical manipulation of the elderly.

definition.def: the control or use of something in a way that shows skill
the skill or act of moving a person's bones or joints into the correct position
examples: manipulation of the bones of the back

examples.sentence: Consequently, an increasing number of scientists are beginning to explore the alternative of geo-engineering - a term which generally refers to the intentional large-scale manipulation of the environment.
In other studies, such as one by Alison Ames in 2008, polar bears showed deliberate and focused manipulation.
As expected, only about one-third of the participants detected this manipulation.
